verdict.rationale: Lambda's On-Demand Cloud provides GPU-backed VMs that can be deployed self-serve 'in minutes' and launched programmatically via a live, key-gated REST API. Instances come with Lambda Stack and JupyterLab preinstalled and are reachable over SSH, and a community user reports signing up and running a GH200 in Jupyter. missing for 10: an independent measurement of launch-to-ready time, and explicit documentation of the console launch steps (console launch is only implied via the Instances page).

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: Deploy NVIDIA B200, H100, A100, or GH200 instances in minutes with self-serve, first-come access.
You can also launch instances programmatically by using the Lambda Cloud API.
On-Demand Cloud (ODC) provides on-demand access to Linux-based, GPU-backed virtual machine instances.
You can connect to your On-Demand Cloud (ODC) instances directly through SSH or by using the preinstalled JupyterLab server.
Lambda also preinstalls Lambda Stack, a standard set of AI/ML-related drivers, tools, and frameworks, on the instance
